text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today after hitting a near two-week high yesterday, as oil prices retreated from their Monday spike. Brent crude had jumped above $109 on Monday following Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, but that geopolitical premium appears to have cooled somewhat—the stock gained 3.8% yesterday on the news but gave back a small portion of those gains today as immediate market reaction faded.

The broader backdrop remains supportive for an oil major like this one. The gap between world oil prices ($126.55) and U.S. prices ($101.55) is historically wide, and a recent analysis flagged that physical delivery costs alone add roughly $38 per barrel when accounting for surging tanker rates—meaning the "real" cost of oil to refineries and importers is substantially higher than headline prices suggest. This structural tightness in global oil supply and logistics continues to underpin energy stocks despite today's modest pullback.
